subject: Post-call: ClearShore technical debrief & next steps (SLOs / topology)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire Wong <claire@clearshore.io>, Alex Becker <alex.becker@clearshore.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: ClearShore technical debrief & initial SLO mapping

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. I wanted to capture the key items we agreed on, confirm a few open questions, and propose next steps so everyone has the same view. Please holler if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points / goals you shared
- Real-time triage scoring for incoming prior-auth requests; 95th pct latency target critical for UX (clinician-facing).
- Peak traffic pattern: regular daytime load ~120 qps, scheduled spikes to ~250 qps for batch ingest windows; occasional short bursts toward 500 qps during operational flushes.
- Must meet HIPAA constraints and allow a private deployment option (VPC/on-prem evaluation needed).
- Long-context documents (6k–8k tokens) for chart summarization and extraction.

Initial SLOs we sketched during the call
- Latency: p95 <= 250 ms for a 2k–4k token typical request; p99 target ~450 ms (soft).
- Throughput: sustained baseline 180–220 qps, burst up to 500 qps with autoscaling/burst.
- Availability: target 99.9% for POC, will iterate for contract SLA.

Model / inference notes
- Baseline model: quantized 7B-class model (int8) for first pass; quality fallback to a 13B variant for hard cases.
- Need KV/prefix caching for repeated patient prompts to avoid hitting cold KV on common templates.
- Must support 8k context across the pipeline; discuss chunking + retrieval vs single-token-context approaches.

Topology options (short list)
- Hosted (fastest): Redwood hosted API for initial validation — faster time to POC, limited private controls.
- Dedicated pool: reserved GPU fleet (Redwood Dedicated) for predictable throughput and isolation.
- Private (VPC): customer-controlled VPC with private control plane — required for HIPAA sign-off if procurement demands.

Open questions for ClearShore
1) Procurement timeline (approx date when PO/contract review completes)?
2) Expected 90-day data-retention policy and any special audit requirements beyond SOC2/HIPAA?
3) Any specific inference hardware constraints (e.g., prefer on-prem A10 vs cloud A100)?

Immediate next steps
- Karthik will draft a short topology & SLO estimate (attachments: topology sketch + cost SLO workbook).
- Redwood to share SOC2 summary + HIPAA addendum and a mutual action plan (MOP) link.
- Schedule a 60-minute deep-dive with ClearShore infra/security to align on VPC/networking (proposal: week of Mar 24).

Attachments: clearshore_topology_v1.pdf (topology sketch), redwood_slo_estimate_v1.xlsx (ballpark sizing/cost).

Thanks — Soojin

--

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: ClearShore technical debrief & initial SLO mapping

Thanks Soojin — this looks right and helpful. A few clarifications from our side so you can refine the estimate: 

- Procurement: legal gets the initial SOW this week; we expect the internal procurement review to finish by 31 Mar (target).
- Compliance: HIPAA baseline required. We also need information on encryption-at-rest key management — our security team prefers KMS/HSM integration.
- Data retention: we want patient-level logs purged at 90 days, but audit logs for model inferences stored for 1 year (redacted PII where possible).
- Context: many of our documents exceed 6k tokens; we want an approach that avoids severe latency spikes for long docs (so chunk+retrieval is probably fine but please include cost delta for chunking vs single-pass long-context).

A couple of asks: 
1) Can you provide a ballpark monthly cost range for a POC (approx 2–3 weeks of steady traffic at 180 qps + bursts)? We need this for the procurement packet.
2) Is a private VPC deployment required for HIPAA or is a Dedicated (customer-isolated) cluster acceptable? Our security team will weigh in but an early opinion helps.

We'll plan to set the infra deep-dive after your topology doc. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Claire

Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2025 08:47:00 +0000
Subject: Technical follow-up: topology options + SLO sizing (draft)

Hi Claire / Alex — following Soojin's recap, I sketched a conservative sizing and a recommended topology for the POC. High-level notes below; attached is the topology sketch and an SLO sizing workbook.

SLO mapping & assumptions- p95 target: 220 ms (2k token typical payload)- p99 target: 420–500 ms (depends on cold KV footprint)- Baseline sustained throughput: 180–220 qps; target burst support to 500 qps with autoscale bursting

Recommended POC topology (minimum to validate latency/throughput)
- Dedicated GPU pool (recommended for POC): 6x A100-40GB equivalents (sharded model instances + batching). This configuration balances headroom and cost; we expect it to sustain ~200–240 qps at p95~220ms with int8 quantized 7B models and KV cache enabled.
- Fallback path: 2x 13B-class instances (int8) for safety for <10% of requests that need higher quality; route via smart-routing policy so cost is bounded.
- KV cache & prefix cache: deploy local KV on each serving node; set warm-up policy for frequent patient contexts to avoid p99 penalties.
- Batching policy: adaptive continuous batching with 8–16 token windows for throughput-sensitive endpoints; keep tail latency budget for clinician UI endpoints.

Long-context approach- Prefer hybrid: retrieval + chunked processing for very long records (8k+ tokens) — single-pass 8k contexts increase memory footprint and cost by ~1.6x. We'll include an explicit cost delta in the workbook.

Security / compliance notes
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports KMS integrations; for POC we can offer Customer-Managed Keys in Dedicated or Private modes.
- Audit logs: we can export inference traces to your SIEM; redact PII at ingest as needed.

Ballpark POC cost (very rough)
- Dedicated 6xA100-40GB baseline + 2x13B fallback for 30 days of testing: estimated $65k–$95k total (includes infra + inference usage + support). We'll tighten this after we get exact QPS profiles and context-length histograms.

Next steps (technical)
1) Soojin: share MOP link + SOC2/HIPAA docs.
2) ClearShore: provide token-length distribution (sample histogram) and expected burst cadence so we can refine estimate.
3) Schedule infra deep-dive (networking/VPC) week of Mar 24 — propose Mar 25 16:00 PT.

Attachments: clearshore_topology_v1.pdf, redwood_slo_estimate_v1.xlsx, clearshore_mop_draft.xlsx

Thanks — Karthik
